nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: there is no disagreement about pronouncing it with sukūn (vowellessness). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: it was given sukūn because these are letters of spelling, in which the pause is intended. The people of Medina read it between tafkhīm (full pronunciation) and imāla (inclination toward "e"). Muḥammad ibn Saʿdān related from Abū Muḥammad from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ that he read كهيعص with the yā inclined (imāla), the hā between tafkhīm and imāla, and the ṣād assimilated. Abū ʿUbayd reported that Ḥamza used to incline the yā and pronounce the hā fully, and that ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī used to give kasra-inclination to both the hā and the yā. Khārija reported that al-Ḥasan used to pronounce kāf with ḍamma; someone else reported that he used to pronounce «hā» with ḍamma; and Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq reported that al-Ḥasan used to pronounce yā with ḍamma. Abū Ḥātim said: ḍamma is not permissible on the kāf, nor on the hā, nor on the yā. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The reading of the people of Medina is among the best there is on this. Imāla is permissible in «hā» and «yā» and what resembles them, such as bā, tā and thā when shortened; this is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. He said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān told me that the Basrans are alone in discussing imāla, and that the Kufans did not mention it as they mentioned other parts of grammar. Imāla is permissible, according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl, in what we have mentioned only because these are names of what is written, so they distinguished between them and particles such as «لا» and «ما»; whoever inclines any of these [particles] is in error, and likewise «ما» meaning «which» (الذي). He does not permit «حتّى» to be inclined, nor «إلّا» of exception, because both are particles; but if you name something with them, imāla becomes permissible. They (the two) permitted it in «أنّى» because it is an adverbial noun, like أين and كيف. Imāla of «kāf» is not permissible because the alif is in the middle. As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, it has puzzled a number of people, so that they said it is not permissible, among them Abū Ḥātim. The correct account of it is what Hārūn the reader explained.
He said: al-Ḥasan used to give a trace (ishmām) of the ḍamma — meaning that he would hint at it, just as Sībawayh reported that some Arabs say الصلاة and الزكاة hinting toward the wāw; and for this reason they are written in the muṣḥafs with wāw.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
قالَ آيَتُكَ: mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (أن) with its ṣila. تُكَلِّمَ: accusative by أن, because «لا» does not intervene [as a barrier]. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted «أن لا تكلّمُ الناس» in the nominative, meaning «that you will not speak to people» (أنك لا تكلم الناس), as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 282-
ألا زعمت بسباسة اليوم أنّني ... كبرت وأن لا يشهد اللهو أمثالي
(Basbāsa claimed today that I have grown old, and that men like me do not attend amusement.)
Al-Akhfash said: سَوِيًّا is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: he refrains from speech in this condition.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: فَأَوْحى إِلَيْهِمْ أَنْ سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا: two adverbials (ẓarf). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that العشيّ is feminine, and may be masculine when used vaguely. He said: العشيّ may also be the plural of عشيّة.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: يا يَحْيى خُذِ الْكِتابَ بِقُوَّةٍ: from أخذ يأخذ. The original is أؤخذ; the second hamza was dropped because of frequent use — and it was said, because two guttural letters come together — and the [initial] hamza was then dispensed with, and the dhāl was given kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. وَآتَيْناهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا: as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
وَحَناناً: conjoined to الحكم. There are two views from Ibn ʿAbbās on its meaning. One, he said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, inclined toward him with mercy; the other view: the mercy toward people he was given, so that he might rescue them from disbelief and evil. وَزَكاةً: there are two views on its meaning. One is that he was given increase and growth in good; the other is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, declared him pure by describing him as pure and God-fearing, for He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَكانَ تَقِيًّا.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
وَسَلامٌ عَلَيْهِ
Nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite noun is acceptable because it carries the meaning of a supplication.
The meaning of «سلام عليك» and «سلام الله عليك» is the same in the language.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ: there are three views on its nominative case. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is nominative by كهيعص. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: this is impossible, because «كهيعص» is not among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about Zakariyyā; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave information about him and about the good news He gave him, and «كهيعص» is not part of his story. Al-Akhfash said:
the implied meaning is: «Among what We relate to you is the mention of the mercy of your Lord». The third view is that the meaning is: «This which We recite to you is the mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant». رحمة is written with hāʾ, and one pauses on it [with hāʾ], and likewise everything like it. We know of no disagreement among the grammarians on this, outside poetry; indeed they have argued that this hāʾ is for the feminine of nouns, and distinguished between it and [the tāʾ of] verbs.
Al-Akhfash said: عَبْدَهُ is accusative by رحمة (the maṣdar). زَكَرِيَّا is a badal (substitute) for it, and it is a diptote because it contains the alif of the feminine. This is for whoever makes it a derived Arabic word, who does not inflect it as triptote either as definite or indefinite; whoever makes it a foreign word inflects it as triptote when indefinite.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: إِذْ: in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). نادى رَبَّهُ نِداءً: an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun). خَفِيًّا: its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ الْعَظْمُ مِنِّي: the imperfect is يهن, originally يوهن; the wāw was dropped because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra. وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْباً: there are two views on its accusative. One is that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of اشتعل is «became white-haired» (شاب); this is the view of al-Akhfash Saʿīd. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: it is accusative as tamyīz (specification). The view of al-Akhfash is preferable, because it is derived from a verb, and [treating it as] a maṣdar suits it better. وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا: [شقيا is] the khabar (predicate) of أكن.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
وَإِنِّي خِفْتُ الْمَوالِيَ مِنْ وَرائِي: [الموالي is] accusative by خفت. The yāʾ was given a vowel in the accusative position because of its lightness, and given sukūn in the nominative and genitive positions because of their heaviness. It is related that ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, read خفّت الموالي من ورائي («the kinsmen have become few after me»); this is an irregular (shādhdh) reading, related only by Kaʿb, the client of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from Saʿīd from ʿUthmān, and it is very far-fetched. Some scholars have claimed it is not permissible.
He said: how could he say «the kinsmen have become few after my death» while he is alive? The interpretation of it is that by «من ورائي» he does not mean «after my death» but «behind me» at that time. This too is far-fetched; it would need evidence that they had become few and scarce at that time, whereas Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has told about them what indicates their great number, when they said: «Which of them will take charge of Maryam?» وَكانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عاقِراً: that is, she does not give birth, as though she had a wound (ʿaqr).
The verb from it, عقرت, is heard from the Arabs, and the analogical form is عقرت. «[Translator's note: the two forms are written identically without vowels in the source; presumably ʿaqurat as heard and ʿaqarat as analogical, or vice versa.]» فَهَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا: the imperfect is يهب, originally يوهب with kasra on the hāʾ. Whoever says the original is يوهب with fatḥa on the hāʾ is mistaken, because if it were as he says, the wāw would not have been dropped, just as it is not dropped in يوجل. The wāw was dropped only because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra; then [the hāʾ] was given fatḥa after its dropping because it contains one of the guttural letters.
The people of the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), al-Ḥasan, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ with both in the nominative; Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, Abū ʿAmr, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read يرثْني ويرثْ من آل يعقوب with both in the jussive. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading, with the nominative, is preferable and better in Arabic, and the argument for it is what Abū ʿUbayd said, for his argument is good. He said: the meaning is:
«Grant me from Yourself the heir (walī) whose condition and description is this», because among heirs (awliyāʾ) there are some who do not inherit; so he said:
«Grant the one who will be my heir». He rejected the jussive because its meaning is «if You grant him to me he will inherit from me» — so how could he inform Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of this when He knows it better than he does? This is a cogent argument, because the answer to an imperative, according to the grammarians, carries the meaning of condition and requital. You say: أطع الله جلّ وعزّ يدخلك الجنة («obey Allah, Mighty and Majestic, [and] He will admit you to Paradise»), meaning: «if you obey Him, He will admit you to Paradise». As for the meaning of يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ, the scholars have three answers on it:
It was said: it is inheritance of prophethood; it was said: it is inheritance of wisdom; and it was said: it is inheritance of wealth. As for their saying "inheritance of prophethood", it is impossible, because prophethood is not inherited; if it were inherited, someone would say: all people are descended from Nūḥ, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he was a prophet sent [as messenger]. Inheritance of wisdom and knowledge is a good position; in the ḥadīth: «The scholars are the heirs of the prophets». As for inheritance of wealth, it is not excluded, even though some people have denied it on account of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity». There is no proof in this, because a single person may speak of himself in the plural; and this may be interpreted as meaning «what we have left as charity is not inherited», because the Prophet ﷺ did not leave behind anything to be inherited from him; rather, what was his was something Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made permissible for him during his lifetime, by His saying, Majestic and Mighty: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ [al-Anfāl: 41], since the meaning of «for Allah, Mighty and Majestic» is «for the ways of Allah, exalted be His praise», and among the ways of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is what serves the interest of the Messenger ﷺ as long as he lives. If it is said: in some narrations there is «We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is charity», then both interpretations apply to it: that «ما» means «which» (الذي), and the other, that one whose condition is this is not inherited from. مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ: [يعقوب] is a diptote because it is foreign. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī claimed that if they said it was another Yaʿqūb, other than Yaʿqūb son of Isḥāq, he would inflect it as triptote; and he said: they did say that he is other than Yaʿqūb son of Isḥāq, peace be upon them both.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: يا زَكَرِيَّا: a singular (mufrad) vocative. اسْمُهُ يَحْيى: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). يحيى is a diptote because it was originally an imperfect verb; it is written with yāʾ to distinguish it from the verb. لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا: we have already mentioned it. It has also been said that its meaning is: We did not command anyone before you to name his son Yaḥyā. «[Translator's note: the source shifts to the second person ("before you") here; translated as written.]»

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
أَنَّى: in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا: Qatāda said:
that is, in age; and the implied form in Arabic is: «an extreme age» (سنّا عتيّا). The original is عتوّا, because it is from the roots with wāw; the wāw was replaced by yāʾ because it is its sister and lighter than it, and because the verses [rhyme] on yāʾ. Whoever read عِتِيًّا [with kasra on the ʿayn] disliked the ḍamma together with the kasra and the yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: قالَ كَذلِكَ قالَ رَبُّكَ: the kāf is in the position of the nominative, i.e. «the matter is thus». هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ: al-Farrāʾ said: that is, creating him is easy for Me. The people of Medina, the people of Basra and ʿĀṣim read وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ, and the rest of the Kufans read وقد خلقناك. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading is closer to the written text (sawād) [of the muṣḥaf].

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
فَأَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْها رُوحَنا
This is Jibrāʾīl (Gabriel), peace be upon him. He was called a rūḥ (spirit) because he brings the revelation by which the servants are given life; since what he brings gives the servants life, he was called a rūḥ. For this reason ʿĪsā (Jesus) ﷺ was also called a rūḥ. فَتَمَثَّلَ لَها بَشَراً سَوِيًّا
As a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
قالَ إِنَّما أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلاماً زَكِيًّا (19) قالَ إِنَّما أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ
A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). لِأَهَبَ لَكِ
 is the reading of most people, and it is the sound transmission from Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym. Abū ʿUbayd, Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq and others among the people of precise transmission reported this — except Warsh, who transmitted from him «ليهب»; and the reading of Abū ʿAmr is «ليهب», with no disagreement from him. Abū ʿUbayd said: This contradicts all the copies of the Qurʾān, every one of them. He said: If it were permissible to change one letter of the muṣḥaf by personal opinion, it would be permissible in others. He said: This would amount to transforming the Qurʾān until what was revealed of it could not be distinguished from what was not. Abū Jaʿfar said: «ليهب» allows two interpretations. One: that he intends «لأهب» and then lightens the hamza. The other is without lightening the hamza, its meaning being: "He sent me so that He may give (ليهب)." As for one who reads «لأهب», its implied form is: "He said: so that I may give," because in His saying إِنَّما أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ
there is what indicates this.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي The doubling (taḍʿīf) appears overtly because the second letter is vowelless. بَشَرٌ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا The original form is «أكن», and we have mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَكانَ أَمْراً مَقْضِيًّا The original form is «مقضويّ»; then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: A ẓarf (adverb of place); or, if you wish, it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "she made for a distant place (مكانا قصيا)."

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: فَأَجاءَهَا الْمَخاضُ إِلى جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ It was said: because she sought the shade. قالَتْ يا لَيْتَنِي مِتُّ For one who reads «متّ» (with kasra) there are two views on its derivation. One is that it is from «متّ أمات», like «خفت أخاف». The other is the view of Sībawayh, that it is from «متّ أموت»; Sībawayh claimed that there occur in the speech of the Arabs, on the pattern faʿiltu – afʿulu, «فضل يفضل» and «متّ تموت», and no others are known. وَكُنْتُ نَسْياً مَنْسِيًّا is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read وَكُنْتُ نَسْياً with fatḥa on the nūn. Abū Jaʿfar said: The kasra of the nūn here is preferable in Arabic for two reasons. One is that the fatḥa form is a maṣdar (verbal noun) while the kasra form is a noun, and the noun is preferable here to the maṣdar. The other reason is that the Arabs use the maṣdar here on the pattern fiʿlān, saying «نسيت نسيانا».

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: فَناداها مِنْ تَحْتِها As for the people of Medina, the people of Kufa and the people of Basra — except al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr, al-Nakhaʿī and ʿĀṣim — they read «من تحتها» with fatḥa on the mīm. Abū ʿUbayd claimed that for one who reads «من تحتها», it is possible in his reading that it refers to Jibrāʾīl ﷺ and to ʿĪsā, peace be upon him; and one who reads «من تحتها» takes it to refer to ʿĪsā ﷺ specifically. [Translator's note: the source gives «من تحتها» unvowelled both times; the first presumably intends «مِنْ تَحْتِها» (preposition) and the second «مَنْ تَحْتَها» (relative noun), though the preceding sentence attributes the fatḥa reading to the majority.] Abū Jaʿfar said: «من» is a noun and «تحتها» is a ẓarf (adverb), and nothing prevents its meaning from referring to Jibrāʾīl ﷺ, just as in the first.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
There are six readings of it. The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read تُساقِطْ with tāʾ and a doubled sīn [Translator's note: i.e. «تَسَّاقَطْ»]. Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «تساقط» with tāʾ and a light (undoubled) sīn. Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib read «يسّاقط» with yāʾ and a doubled sīn. Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ read «تسقط». The two remaining readings are تُساقِطْ and «نساقط». Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading has the original form «تتساقط», then the tāʾ was assimilated into the sīn; the second is by omission (of one tāʾ); and the third is by assimilation, and omission is not permissible with it. The accusative of «رطب» in these three readings is as a specification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz), as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 283-
فلو أنّها نفس تموت سويّة ... ولكنّها نفس تساقط أنفسا
(If only it were one soul that dies all at once — but it is a soul that falls away soul by soul.)
Abū Isḥāq reported from Abū al-ʿAbbās that it is accusative through «هزّي». The fourth reading takes it as accusative through «تسقط» or through «هزّي», and likewise the fifth. Abū Isḥāq said: One who reads «نساقط» means: "We cause to fall upon you fresh ripe dates, so that this may be a sign." Abū Jaʿfar said: «الرطب» is treated as masculine with the sense of the genus and as feminine with the sense of a collective.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْناً Abū Isḥāq said: "Eat of the fresh dates and drink of the water."
He said: عَيْناً is accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Abū Jaʿfar said: The original form is «أأكلي» with two hamzas; one of them was omitted because they came together and because of frequent use. By analogy the second should have been lightened and become a wāw, so that one would say «أوكل», just as one says «أوجر فلان» from «الأجر». When the second hamza was omitted, the first was no longer needed, so it was said «كلي». The nūn was dropped because the verb is not inflected (muʿrab) — and, according to the Kufans, because of the jussive (jazm) — and likewise «واشربي» and «وقرّي». Al-Aṣmaʿī said: «قررت به عينا» is derived from «القرّ» (coolness), i.e. my eye became cool and did not shed tears so as to become hot. Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said: It is from «قررت في المكان» (I settled in the place), i.e. my eye settled and slept and did not stay awake. It was also said: its meaning is "I became calm (هدأت)" when I attained what I had been longing for. فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ is in the position of a jussive (jazm) by the condition. The original form is «فإما تريي»; the nūn was added for emphasis, and this was acceptable in a statement because «ما» entered. Sībawayh reported ] «بألم ما تختننّه» [Translator's note: the bracket is as in the source]. If it were pronounced without the nūn it would be «فإما ترى»; when you added the nūn you restored it to its original form, and the yāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters — the kasra being preferable in order to distinguish the masculine from the feminine. Then the hamza was lightened: its vowel was cast onto the rāʾ and it was dropped, so it became «ترين». فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا Derived from «آنس», when one knows and perceives; the «إنسيّ» is one who is seen and known. The plural is «أناسي»: an alif is added in third position, as is done in plurals, so you say «بختيّ» and «بخاتيّ»; and that is frequent and well known.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: فَأَتَتْ بِهِ قَوْمَها تَحْمِلُهُ In the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
يا أُخْتَ هارُونَ A muḍāf (genitive construct) munādā (one addressed in the vocative). The original form is «أخوة»; this is shown by «أخوات». Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: The wāw was omitted to distinguish what is attached (mutashabbith) from what is not attached. We do not know of anyone who preceded Abū al-ʿAbbās to this view, despite its excellence and soundness. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the hamza was given ḍamma in their saying «أخت», and the bāʾ was given kasra in their saying «بنت», only to distinguish what had a wāw omitted from what had a yāʾ omitted: the ḍamma is the sign of the wāw and the kasra the sign of the yāʾ. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd stated that this view is mistaken.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Concerning His saying «يا أخت هارون» the scholars hold two views. One is that Hārūn was a righteous man, so they said "O sister of Hārūn," i.e. "O you who resemble him in righteousness"; the believers are brothers only in this sense, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established brotherhood among his Companions. Jaʿfar transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that there was a dissolute man called Hārūn, so they said to her: "O sister of Hārūn." Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is preferable because there is a ḥadīth with a connected chain (musnad) for it.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
قالُوا كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَنْ كانَ فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا There are three views on it. One is that «كان» is redundant (zāʾida) and صَبِيًّا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the operator governing it being the implied "being settled" (al-istiqrār). It was also said: «كان» means "occurred," and «صبيّ» is accusative as a ḥāl, except that the operator governing it is «كان». The third view is that of Abū Isḥāq. He said:
«من» is for the condition, and the meaning is: "Whoever was in the cradle a child, how shall we speak to him?" He said: It is as you say, "Whoever neither hears nor sees, how shall I address him?" Abū Jaʿfar said: The grammarians needed these interpretations only because all people were once children in the cradle, and ʿĪsā ﷺ must be distinguished from them by something. Sībawayh reported the redundancy of «كان» and recited: [al-Wāfir] 284-
فكيف إذا مررت بدار قوم ... وجيران لنا كانوا كرام
(How, then, when I pass by the abode of a people, and neighbours of ours who were noble?)
And the grammarians reported «ما كان أحسن زيدا» ("How handsome Zayd was!"), and they spoke of «كان» being cancelled (ilghāʾ).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: قالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتانِيَ الْكِتابَ There are two views on its meaning. One: He decreed that He would give it to me. The other: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, perfected his intellect, gave him the Book and made him a prophet while he was in the cradle. Qatāda said: «في المهد» means "in the lap."

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: وَجَعَلَنِي مُبارَكاً أَيْنَ ما Derived from «البركة» (blessing), which is steadfastness in good. He was steadfast in good, grown up [Translator's note: «مشبا» as in the source; reading uncertain]. As ʿAmr ibn Qays said: the meaning of «وجعلني مباركا» is "a teacher who instructs in good conduct." What makes this clear is what Shuʿba transmitted from ʿAlqama ibn Marthad, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbayda, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿUthmān, from the Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: the text of this ḥadīth is not given in the source]; and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq transmitted from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "The best of you is the one who learns the Qurʾān and teaches it." And Sharīk transmitted from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The best of you is the one who learns the Qurʾān and teaches it to be recited." وَأَوْصانِي بِالصَّلاةِ وَالزَّكاةِ Abū Isḥāq said: «الزكاة» is purity. Others said: "And He enjoined upon me zakāt" means that I pay it when it becomes due upon me and command it. ما دُمْتُ حَيًّا The khabar (predicate) of «دمت», and a ḥāl (circumstantial) according to al-Farrāʾ.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: وَبَرًّا بِوالِدَتِي Al-Kisāʾī said: It is conjoined (nasaq) to «مبارك», i.e. "and He made me dutiful." Ibn Nahīk read «وبرّ بوالدتي» (genitive), meaning: "and He enjoined upon me prayer and zakāt and dutifulness to my mother."

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّا The last of the words of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. When he spoke in his mother's lap, the sign became manifest to them.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: ذلِكَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ Al-Kisāʾī said: «قول الحقّ» (nominative) is a naʿt (adjective). Abū Ḥātim said: The meaning is "it is the word of truth." It was also said: the implied form is "this speech is the word of truth." ʿĀṣim and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ in the accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: in the sense of "truly (حقّا)." Abū Isḥāq said: It is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "I say the word of truth," because what precedes it indicates this.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
ما كانَ لِلَّهِ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ مِنْ وَلَدٍ «أن» is in the position of a nominative, as the noun (ism) of «كان». مِنْ وَلَدٍ is in the position of an accusative, and «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. The reality of this is that when you say «ما اشتريت فرسا» ("I did not buy a horse"), the meaning may be that you bought nothing at all, and the meaning may be that you bought several horses.
When you say «ما اشتريت فرسين» ("I did not buy two horses"), three meanings are possible: that you bought nothing; that you bought one; and that you bought more than two. But when you say «ما اشتريت من فرس», the meaning becomes that you bought nothing at all of this genus. سُبْحانَهُ A maṣdar (verbal noun). فَإِنَّما يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ is the reading of the majority, and Ibn ʿĀmir the Syrian read «فيكون» [Translator's note: i.e. «فَيَكُونَ» in the accusative; the vowelling is not shown in the source].

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ is the reading of the people of Medina, and the people of Kufa read «وإنّ» with kasra on the hamza, as a resumptive (mustaʾnaf) clause. [Translator's note: so in the source, though the passage then discusses the fatḥa as the alternative.] On the fatḥa there are several views. The doctrine of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them, is that the meaning is "and because (ولأنّ) Allah is my Lord and your Lord"; and likewise, according to them, وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا [al-Jinn: 18]; so «أنّ» is in the position of an accusative according to them. Al-Farrāʾ allowed that it be in the position of a genitive by omission of the lām. He also allowed that it be in the position of a genitive with the meaning "and He enjoined upon me prayer and zakāt, and that Allah is my Lord and your Lord." Al-Kisāʾī allowed that it be in the position of a nominative, meaning "and the matter is that Allah is my Lord and your Lord." There is a fifth view, which Abū ʿUbayd reported that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ held, namely that the meaning is:
"And He decreed that Allah is my Lord and your Lord."

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنا Indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn because its form is the form of the imperative while its meaning is that of wonder (taʿajjub): "How well they hear, and how well they see!"

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ We have already mentioned it. It is transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: There is no one who enters the Fire but that he has a house in Paradise, and he grieves over it. It was also said: the grief occurs when he is given his book in his left hand. And the meaning of إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ is: every person is made to know what is for him and what is against him. It was also said: the implied form is:
"And warn them of the news of the Day of Grief, when the matter is decided," so He informed them that they are to be punished.

nahhas-irab:41-42.t:
إِنَّهُ كانَ صِدِّيقاً نَبِيًّا [«صدّيقا» is] the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and «نبيّا» is a naʿt (adjective) of it; it may also be a second khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun.
Abū Isḥāq said: The pause on إذ قال لأبيه يا أبه is with hāʾ, because it is the hāʾ of the feminine. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: The pause is with tāʾ, because it is annexed to what cannot be separated, just as you say «هذه نعمتي». Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned this in Sūrat Yūsuf at greater length. Al-Kisāʾī said: «عصيّ» and «عاصي» are the same.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t:
قالَ أَراغِبٌ Nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أنت» is a fāʿil (agent) that stands in place of the khabar (predicate), just as you say «أقائم أنت؟».
Beginning with an indefinite noun is acceptable because of what precedes it [i.e. the interrogative].

nahhas-irab:47-47.t:
قالَ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكَ Beginning with the indefinite noun is acceptable because it carries the meaning of the accusative, and in this place it carries the meaning of parting and leaving. Similar is وَإِذا خاطَبَهُمُ الْجاهِلُونَ قالُوا سَلاماً [al-Furqān: 63].
سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي i.e. if you accept Islam and repent. إِنَّهُ كانَ بِي حَفِيًّا ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him: i.e. gracious. Al-Kisāʾī said: one says «حفي به حفاوة وحفوة». Al-Farrāʾ said: «إنه كان بي حفيا» means "knowing, answering me when I call upon Him." Abū Isḥāq said: One says «قد تحفّى فلان بفلان حفوة» when he treats him kindly and dutifully.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ وَما تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ «ما» is in the position of an accusative because it is conjoined (maʿṭūf), i.e. "and I withdraw from what you call upon."

nahhas-irab:50-50.t:
وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ لِسانَ صِدْقٍ i.e. a word of truth, as Aʿshā Bāhila said: [al-Basīṭ] 285-
إنّي أتتني لسان لا أسرّ بها ... من علو لا عجب فيها ولا سخر
(A report [lit. "a tongue"] has come to me in which I take no joy, from on high — no wonder in it and no mockery.)
He treated «اللسان» as feminine in this verse, and that is a known dialect, even though the Qurʾān has come with the masculine.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said عَلِيًّا, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of «لسان». Another poet said: [al-Wāfir] 286-
ندمت على لسان فات منّي ... فليت بيانه في جوف عكم
(I regretted a word [lit. "a tongue"] that escaped me — would that its utterance had stayed inside a sack.)

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: وَقَرَّبْناهُ نَجِيًّا Accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ said: «نجيّ» is like «جليس» (companion in sitting). He said: «نجيّ» and «نجوى» can both be nouns and maṣdars (verbal nouns).

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ مِنْ رَحْمَتِنا أَخاهُ هارُونَ A badal (substitute) from «الأخ». It is a diptote because it is a definite non-Arabic name; likewise «إدريس», peace be upon him.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t:
وَكانَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ مَرْضِيًّا Derived from «الرّضوان». According to Sībawayh, the original form is «مرضوّ»; the wāw was replaced by yāʾ because it is lighter, and likewise «مسنيّة». The wāw was replaced by yāʾ only because there is a ḍamma before it, and the vowelless letter is not a firm barrier. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: One who says «مرضي» built it on «رضيت». They said:
The people of the Ḥijāz say «مرضوّ». There is a third view, which al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported; they said: Some Arabs say «رضوان» and «رضيّان» (as duals), so «رضوان» is based on «مرضوّ» and «رضيّان» on «مرضيّ». The Basrans do not allow anything to be said except «رضوان» and «ربوان». Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say:
They err in spelling, writing «ربا» with yāʾ, and then they err in what is worse than this, writing «ربيان»; nothing is permissible but «ربوان» and «رضوان». Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ رِباً لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ [al-Rūm: 39].

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
خَرُّوا سُجَّداً As a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَبُكِيًّا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; it was also said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and they wept a weeping (بكيّا)."
One says «بكى يبكي بكاء وبكي وبكيّا», except that al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When you shorten «البكاء» (to «البكى»), it is like grief, i.e. it has no sound with it. He (the poet) said: [al-Wāfir] 287-
بكت عيني وحقّ لها بكاها ... وما يغني البكاء ولا العويل ]
(My eye wept, and rightly did it weep — yet what avail are weeping and wailing?) [Translator's note: the closing bracket is as in the source.]

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا «الغيّ» in the language means disappointment (khayba). Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it already.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: إِلَّا مَنْ تابَ In the position of an accusative as an excepted noun (istithnāʾ). Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning may also be "but (لكن) whoever repents." فَأُولئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ وَلا يُظْلَمُونَ شَيْئاً.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ As a badal (substitute). Abū Isḥāq said: «جنّات عدن» (nominative) is also permissible, as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
Abū Ḥātim said: Were it not for the written form, «جنّة عدن» would be permissible, because before it is «يدخلون الجنة». إِنَّهُ كانَ وَعْدُهُ مَأْتِيًّا Al-Kisāʾī said: i.e. it is come to and arrived at. Al-Qutabī [Ibn Qutayba] claimed that «مأتيّا» means «آت» (coming). «مأتيّ» has a hamza because it is from «أتى يأتي»; one who lightens the hamza makes it an alif.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْواً إِلَّا سَلاماً Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: This is the kind of exception in which the excepted is not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). He said: If you wish, it is a badal (substitute), i.e. they hear nothing but "peace." وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيها بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا Two adverbs (ẓarfān). Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. there is apportioned to them in these two times what they need at every hour. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. according to the measures of morning and evening as they are in this world, because there is neither night nor day there; it is only the light of the Throne.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: Al-Akhfash said: لَهُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِينا i.e. before we were created; وَما خَلْفَنا what will be after death; وَما بَيْنَ ذلِكَ since we were created.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: فَاعْبُدْهُ وَاصْطَبِرْ لِعِبادَتِهِ The original form is «اصتبر»; combining the tāʾ and the ṣād was heavy because they differ, so the tāʾ was replaced by ṭāʾ, just as you say «اصطام» from «الصوم».

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: The people of Kufa except ʿĀṣim, the people of Mecca, Abū ʿAmr and Abū Jaʿfar read «أولا يذّكّر الإنسان» [Translator's note: the source text has «أولا يذكر», but the following discussion shows the doubled form «يذّكّر» is meant], and Shuʿba, Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read أَوَلا يَذْكُرُ with the light (undoubled) form. In the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is «أولا يتذكّر»; this reading is by way of explanation (tafsīr), because it contradicts the written form of the muṣḥaf, since the original form of «يذّكّر» is «يتذكر», and the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl. The meaning of «يتذكّر» is "reflect," and the meaning of «يذكر» is "become aware and know."

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: فَوَ رَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَالشَّياطِينَ Conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ and mīm [the pronoun «هم»]; and the devils are those who led them astray. ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّا Accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The original form is «جثوّ»; the wāw was replaced by yāʾ because it is at the end [Translator's note: the source has «ظرف», apparently a slip for «طرف», "at the edge/end"], and change is the norm in plurals. One who says «جثيّ» (with kasra on the jīm) made the kasra follow the kasra.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t:
This is a verse that is difficult in i'rab, because all the readers read أَيُّهُمْ in the nominative except Hārūn the reader, for Sībawayh reported from him «ثمّ لننزعنّ من كلّ شيعة أيّهم» in the accusative, making «لننزعنّ» act on «أيّهم». Abū Isḥāq said: There are three views on the nominative of «أيّهم». Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad said — Sībawayh reported it from him — that it is nominative by way of quotation (ḥikāya), and the meaning according to him is: "Then We shall draw out from every party the one of whom it is said, because of his insolence, 'Which of them was most insolent against the Most Merciful?'" Al-Khalīl recited: [al-Kāmil] 288-
ولقد أبيت من الفتاة بمنزل ... فأبيت لا حرج ولا محروم
(I have spent the night with the young woman in such a station — I spent it [as one of whom it is said]: neither constrained nor deprived.)
i.e. "I spent the night in the position of one of whom it is said: he is neither constrained nor deprived." Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq choosing this view and approving it; he said: because it accords with the meaning given by the people of tafsīr. He claimed that the meaning of «ثم لننزعنّ من كلّ شيعة» is: "Then We shall draw out from every sect the most insolent, then the next most insolent," as though He begins the punishment with the most insolent of them, then the one following him. This is the exact wording of Abū Isḥāq on the meaning of the verse. Yūnus said: «لننزعن» is like the verbs that are cancelled (tulghā), so «أيّهم» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Sībawayh said: «أيّهم» is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it differs from its sisters in omission; for if you said «رأيت الذي أفضل منك» or «من أفضل», it would be bad until you say «من هو أفضل», whereas the omission in «أيّهم» is permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: I know of no grammarian who has not faulted Sībawayh on this. I heard Abū Isḥāq say: It is not clear to me that Sībawayh erred in his Book except in two places, this being one of them. He said:
We know of Sībawayh that he treats «أيّ» as declinable (muʿrab) when it stands alone, because it is annexed [i.e. annexable]; how then can he make it indeclinable when it is annexed?
As far as I know, Abū Isḥāq mentioned only these three views. Abū Jaʿfar said: There are four views on it besides these three that Abū Isḥāq mentioned. Al-Kisāʾī said: «لننزعنّ» acts on the meaning, just as you say «لبست من الثياب» and «أكلت من الطعام», and «لننزعن» does not act on «أيّهم» so as to make it accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is "then We shall draw out by calling," and the meaning of «لننزعن» is "We shall call out," since its meaning is "We shall draw out by calling." Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Bakr ibn Shuqayr reported that some of the Kufans say:
«أيّهم» carries the meaning of condition and requital, and for that reason what precedes it does not act on it; the meaning is: "then We shall draw out from every sect, whether they followed one another or not," just as you say «ضربت القوم أيّهم غضب», meaning "whether they became angry or not." So these are six views. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān relate from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, who said: «أيّهم» is connected with «شيعة», and is nominative for this reason; the meaning is: "then We shall draw out from those who formed parties [to see] which of them…," i.e. from those who cooperated and considered which of them was most insolent against the Most Merciful. This is a good view. Al-Kisāʾī reported that «التشايع» means cooperation. «عتيّا» is by way of specification (bayān).

nahhas-irab:71-72.t:
وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها We have mentioned several views on it. Khālid ibn Maʿdān said: When the people of Paradise enter it, they will say: "Our Lord, You promised us that we would come to the Fire." It will be said to them: "You came to it while it was extinguished."
Abū Jaʿfar said: Among the best things said about it — I mean about the verse — is that the meaning is: "There is none of you but will come to the Resurrection," because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said of the believers: لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها [al-Anbiyāʾ: 102] [Translator's note: the source gives the reference as al-Anbiyāʾ 108; the verse is 21:102], and He, exalted be His praise, said: فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ [al-Māʾida: 69 and al-Anʿām: 48]. What indicates that the implied pronoun refers to the Resurrection is فَوَ رَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ, for the gathering is only at the Resurrection; then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها كانَ عَلى رَبِّكَ حَتْماً مَقْضِيًّا. The noun (ism) of «كان» in it is implied, i.e. "its coming was." As for وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيها جِثِيًّا, the implied pronoun refers to the Fire, because it is within the Resurrection, so He alluded to it since it is within it. This is frequent in eloquent Arabic speech. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī and Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra read ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا with fatḥa on the thāʾ [i.e. «ثَمَّ», "there"], and Ibn Abī Laylā read «ثمّه»:
«ثمّ» (there) is an adverb (ẓarf), except that it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is not specified, so it was made indeclinable as «ذا» was made indeclinable. The hāʾ may be for clarifying the vowel, in which case it is dropped (in connected speech), because the vowel is clear in connected speech; or it may be for the feminine of the "spot" (al-buqʿa), in which case it remains in connected speech as a tāʾ.

nahhas-irab:73-74.t:
خَيْرٌ مَقاماً Accusative as a specification (bayān), and likewise نَدِيًّا, and likewise أَحْسَنُ أَثاثاً. وَرِءْياً has five readings. The people of Medina read «وريّا» without hamza; the people of Kufa and Abū ʿAmr read وَرِءْياً with hamza; Yaʿqūb reported that Ṭalḥa read «وريا» with a single light yāʾ; and Sufyān transmitted from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: «هم أحسن أثاثا وزيّا» with zāy. These are four readings. Abū Isḥāq said: «هم أحسن أثاثا وريئا», with a yāʾ followed by a hamza, is also permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: The reading of the people of Medina here is good, and it has two interpretations. One is that it is from «رأيت», then the hamza was lightened, replaced by a yāʾ, and the yāʾ assimilated. This is also good so that the verse-endings agree, since they are without hamza. On this basis Ibn ʿAbbās said: «الريّ» is appearance. The meaning is: "They are better in furnishings and clothing." The second interpretation is that the meaning is that their skins are well-watered [i.e. fresh] from comfort; then the hamza is not permissible, because it is a maṣdar of «رويت ريّا». In the transmission of Warsh it is «وريّا»; whoever transmitted from him «ورئيا» with hamza, that is on the first interpretation. The reading of the people of Kufa and Abū ʿAmr is from «رأيت» in its original form. The reading of Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, «وريا» with a single light yāʾ, I reckon to be an error; some grammarians claimed that its original form was «ورئيا» and then the hamza was dropped. «الزيّ» is outward appearance. The fifth reading is by metathesis (qalb) of the hamza.
Sībawayh reported «راء» in the sense of «رأى».

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: قُلْ مَنْ كانَ فِي الضَّلالَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ مَدًّا It was said: the meaning is "let him live as long as he wishes, for his destination is death and punishment." حَتَّى إِذا رَأَوْا ما يُوعَدُونَ إِمَّا الْعَذابَ وَإِمَّا السَّاعَةَ. Abū Isḥāq said: This is a badal (substitute) from «ما», and the meaning is: "until, when they see the punishment or the Hour."

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: أَطَّلَعَ الْغَيْبَ The alif is the alif of interrogation, and it carries the sense of rebuke. The connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was omitted because it is no longer needed.

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: There are two interpretations of it. One is that «من» is in the position of a nominative as a badal (substitute) from the wāw, i.e. "none possesses intercession except whoever has taken…." The other interpretation is that «من» is in the position of an accusative as an exception in which the excepted is not of the same kind as the first. The meaning is: "but whoever has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful that He will intercede for him." The meaning according to al-Farrāʾ is: "they do not possess intercession except for (لمن) whoever has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful" — not that the lām is implied, but the meaning according to him is on this basis.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t:
The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read وَلَداً with fatḥa on the wāw and the lām, and the rest of the Kufans read «ولدا» with ḍamma on the wāw and sukūn on the lām. Abū ʿUbayd distinguished between them: he claimed that «الولد» (wuld) applies to the family and the children together. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is rejected against him; none of the lexicographers knows it. «الولد» (walad) and «الولد» (wuld) apply only to a man's child and his child's child, except that «ولد» (walad) is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs, as al-Nābigha said: [al-Basīṭ] 289-
مهلا فداء لك الأقوام كلّهم ... وما أثمّر من مال ومن ولد
(Gently! May all the tribes be your ransom, and all I gather of wealth and of children.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd say: «ولد» (wuld) may be the plural of «ولد» (walad), just as one says «وثن» and «وثن» (wathan / wuthn) and «أسد» and «أسد» (asad / usd); and «ولد» and «ولد» may be plurals with one meaning, as one says «عجم» and «عجم» and «عرب» and «عرب» [i.e. ʿujm / ʿajam and ʿurb / ʿarab].

nahhas-irab:89-89.t: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with fatḥa on the hamza [i.e. «أَدًّا»]. «شيئا أادّا» is also permissible, as you say «رادّا»: one says «أدّ يؤدّ أدّا فهو آدّ», and the noun is «الإدّ», when one comes with something enormous and abhorrent.

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: تَكادُ السَّماواتُ with the feminine of the group, and «يكاد» with the masculine of the plural. «ينفطرن», with yāʾ and nūn, is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza; al-Aʿmash, al-Ḥasan, Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read يَتَفَطَّرْنَ ] with yāʾ and tāʾ [Translator's note: the bracket is as in the source]. The first is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, and he argued from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: إِذَا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ [al-Infiṭār: 1], and He did not say «تفطّرت». Abū Jaʿfar said: «يتفطّرن» with yāʾ and tāʾ is preferable in this place because it carries the sense of intensity, so it is preferable: for they disbelieved, and the heavens almost burst apart and fell upon them as punishment for what they did. وَتَخِرُّ الْجِبالُ هَدًّا A maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of «تخرّ» is "collapse in ruins (تهدّ)."

nahhas-irab:91-91.t: أَنْ is in the position of an accusative according to al-Farrāʾ, with the meaning "because they ascribed" and "from their ascribing." Al-Farrāʾ claimed that al-Kisāʾī said: It is in the position of a genitive.

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: Because nothing resembles Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whereas a man's child resembles him.

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: «آتِي» is written with yāʾ; the original had tanwīn, which was dropped for lightness, and it was annexed (as a muḍāf).

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ according to the wording of «كلّ»; according to the meaning it would be «آتوه».

nahhas-irab:96-97.t: سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ الرَّحْمنُ وُدًّا i.e. in the hearts of the believers. «لدّ» is the plural of «ألدّ», like «أصمّ» and «صمّ».

nahhas-irab:98-98.t: هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ In the position of an accusative. أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزاً i.e. they have died and come to [the recompense of] their deeds.
